corpus: This repository's real .sdd/ tree, taken from the branch under test (`git archive <branch> -- .sdd`). No synthetic fixture is authored: `main` carries a v4-era corpus (no adr/, persisted *_design.md, v4 CONSTITUTION) and `develop` a v5-era one (adr/, task/{ticket}/design-draft.md, v5 CONSTITUTION), so each branch's skills are graded inside their own generation's world for free. Build it with build_sdd_fixture.py, which also re-renders .sdd/AI-SDD-PRINCIPLES.md and .claude/rules/ai-sdd-instructions.md from the branch's own plugin source -- the committed copies track the *installed* plugin (v4 on both branches), so leaving them would hand develop's skills a rulebook they do not implement.
variants: main/without -- main's .sdd/ corpus, skill not loaded
develop/without -- develop's .sdd/ corpus, skill not loaded
measurement: Improvement from main to develop is the difference of lifts: lift(era) = score(era/skill) - score(era/without), and improvement = lift(develop) - lift(main). Raw main/skill vs develop/skill scores are NOT compared directly: the .sdd/ corpus itself differs between the branches, so a raw difference cannot separate 'the skill got better' from 'develop's corpus got richer'. The per-era `without` baseline absorbs corpus difficulty, which is what makes the two lifts comparable. This does not contradict ASSERTION_DESIGN.md's rule against comparing main/without with develop/without -- the quantity compared is the lift, never the bare baseline.
assertion_design: Assertions are version-neutral outcome statements. Before editing them, read .claude/skill-evals/ASSERTION_DESIGN.md -- it is the canonical authority and records which assertion shapes were removed and why.
skill_delta_main_to_develop: +49/-17 lines (PR #116 が PRD レベル ID 形式の解決を id_conventions 参照へ変更し、PR-xxx を削除した分を含む)

evals.prompt:
対象PRD: `.sdd/requirement/spec-design/spec-review.md` の内容を existing-prd-text として使い、以下の新規要求を統合(--amend)してください。テキストのみ返してください（ファイルへの書き込みは不要）。

## Use Case Diagram
（新規追加分）
- Actor: Developer
- 新規Use Case: 修正提案に重大度を付与する — 生成された修正提案のそれぞれに [must] / [recommend] / [nits] のいずれかの重大度ラベルを付与する

## Requirements Analysis
### Functional Requirements
| ID | Requirement | Derived From | Priority | Risk | Verification |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| FR_002 | システムは生成する修正提案の重大度を [must] / [recommend] / [nits] の3段階から選択して固定的に付与する | UR_003 | Should | Medium | Demonstration |

## Requirements Diagram
```mermaid
requirementDiagram
functionalRequirement SuggestSeverity {
  id: FR_002
  text: "生成する修正提案の重大度を [must] / [recommend] / [nits] の3段階から選択して固定的に付与する"
  risk: medium
  verifymethod: demonstration
}
FR_002 - derives -> UR_003
```

（注: FR_002 という番号は、既存の FR_001 の最大値を単純に+1した機械的な継続値であり、実際のパイプラインでは呼び出し元 generate-prd Step 3.5 が同じ規則で計算して渡す値。UR_003 は本 PRD の親 PRD（[index.md](../index.md)）が保持する ID で、本 PRD 自身は PRD レベルの UR を持たず FR_001 と同様に親の UR_003 から直接派生する。finalize-prd の評価としてこの番号自体に創作的な意味はない。）
evals.expected_output: The existing text preserved byte-for-byte, the given FR_002 (and only that, nothing invented) inserted at the structurally correct positions in both the requirements diagram and the detail tables, with the new use case reflected in the Use Case Diagram section as well.
files: The prompt inlines actual usecase-text/analysis-text/diagram-text content (finalize-prd's --amend Input contract marks all three as Required and instructs the skill to treat an absent/empty one as a caller error and return existing-prd-text unchanged rather than inventing content -- see finalize-prd/SKILL.md ## Input and Integration Rule 7), so this eval exercises finalize-prd's actual merge/insertion behavior instead of tripping its own missing-input guard and returning a no-op. The FR_002 numbering is a mechanical continuation of the existing PRD's FR_001 max-per-prefix -- per finalize-prd/SKILL.md Integration Rule 5, this is something the caller (generate-prd Step 3.5) computes, not a value finalize-prd or this eval's author invents. This PRD (spec-review.md) derives FR_001 directly from the parent PRD's UR_003 and carries no PRD-level UR of its own, so the new FR_002 does the same -- no new UR row is expected. Any concrete ID shown here (or in other skills' evals/fixtures) is only a representative sample of that mechanical computation, not an endorsed convention -- actual ID format is resolved per id_conventions_config.md.
